summary: Frontend-only check of the Teleton intro modal on / at Android 412x915, iOS 390x844 and Desktop 1920x1080, using Playwright with separate mobile contexts (mobile UA, is_mobile, touch). Every requested check passed.

android_412x915.headline: y=695 to 762
android_412x915.doar_btn: x=27 y=789 h=38 w=185 bottom=827 (88px from base)

ios_390x844.headline: y=636 to 700
ios_390x844.doar_btn: x=25 y=725 h=36 w=173 bottom=761 (83px from base)

critical_code_review_comments: App.js: isMobile starts as false and is set in useEffect, so on mobile the X button is rendered for one frame before it is hidden. Could initialize with useState(() => window.matchMedia('(max-width: 1024px)').matches).

Breakpoints differ: the X is hidden at max-width 1024px, but the iframe mobile layout uses max-aspect-ratio 4/5. On tablet landscape (e.g. 1024x768) the desktop layout shows without the X; the user can still close via DOAR AGORA. Not tested.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mobile layout: logo top-left, headline at the bottom just above a smaller DOAR AGORA button (about 85px from the base), no X button. Clicking DOAR AGORA in the same-origin iframe (frame url contains teleton-intro) removes home-donate-modal-overlay and stays on /, with home-aacd-frame and mobile-confirm-donation-btn visible. Desktop: X is present and closes the modal; DOAR AGORA also closes it.
